guard_streams.source: QMI for BDUK Delivery Performance annual 2025/26

facts.detail: BDUK uses Ofcom premises- and postcode-level data to estimate subsidised premises that are in Ofcom's premises base.
The QMI defines a UPRN as a unique identifier for an addressable location that does not change over time.
BDUK's premises base differs from Ofcom's premises base.
BDUK includes child premises such as apartments in houses of multiple occupation, while Ofcom does not include the individual apartments in its base.
BDUK states that incomplete Ofcom UPRN-level data means it can only reliably compare using Ofcom postcode-level data.

guard_streams.source: QMI for BDUK Delivery Performance annual 2025/26

facts.detail: A premises is classified as passed when a gigabit-capable service can be ordered at the supplier's standard price and connected in the standard timescale.
Overspill means premises not directly funded that received connections as a result of BDUK-funded projects.
Overbuild means a commercial supplier had already provided approved gigabit-capable broadband when the BDUK-subsidised supplier built.
GIS contracted premises are excluded where evidence shows another supplier had already built them.
Approximately 27,065 premises, about 15.7% of GIS delivery, were removed as overbuild, leaving 139,490 reported GIS premises.

guard_streams.source: QMI for BDUK Delivery Performance annual 2025/26

facts.detail: BDUK deduplicates UPRNs within and across interventions.
Where a premises benefits from more than one intervention, the record with the earliest verified delivery date is retained.
Approximately 10,570 premises were removed where records overlapped more than one intervention.
Of those removals, 7,060, or 67%, related to indirect subsidy.
The remaining 3,510, or 33%, involved direct subsidy overlaps, product-level deduplication or data inconsistencies.

guard_streams.source: QMI for BDUK Delivery Performance annual 2025/26

facts.detail: The voucher intervention subsidises otherwise uncommercial broadband build through demand aggregation.
BDUK funds voucher premises where the occupier takes a gigabit-capable service and claims a voucher.
BDUK validates supplier-returned UPRNs and counts premises its cost model identifies as uncommercial due to high costs.
A 5% attrition rate based on Ofcom data is applied to confirm that expected premises have been built.
Where expected-premises data is unavailable or poor, BDUK uses a multiplier method adjusted by an 18% attrition rate.

facts.detail: The QMI says a built premises can take up to six months to appear in BDUK reporting.
BDUK cannot precisely compare its premises base with Ofcom's premises base.
BDUK cannot precisely determine when a premises first received a gigabit-capable connection.
This limitation creates a likely overcount where an unsubsidised supplier built commercially before the subsidised supplier.
Around 7,000 legacy Superfast premises have validated delivery but no supplier-held connection date.
